scope: Proposition 11.6 (Tiled presentations) of the manuscript “Eventual categoricity for abstract elementary classes” (preprints/Eventual-Categoricity-for-Abstract-Elementary-Classes-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 240 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dcb7401285f5ac78), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 89. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let L be admissible and let µ be sufficiently large for the pointed pregeometry and the no-proper-pair conclusion. The order template E gives a presentation in GL as follows. Choose a fixed initial order carrying the whole enumeration of M0. For each active label t, choose a tile Tt, preceded by a buffer Bt, and concatenate these finitely many pairs after the initial order, in any fixed order. Every tile and buffer is a dense linear order without endpoints of size µ. In vertex s retain the initial order, all buffers, and just the tiles with labels t ⊆ s. These presentations have the following properties. 1. Each active relative piece has rank µ. 2. Order embeddings of the corresponding tiles and buffers, fixing the initial pointed data, induce arrows, including between different eligible levels. 3. A presentation has an extension by an arrow gaining µ independent complementary coordi- nates at every active label simultaneously. 4. Tiles may be chosen with µ pairwise disjoint convex substrips, each of size µ. Further insertions of such substrips preserve the preceding assertions and the naturalness of the underlying K-diagrams. No categoricity assumption about GL is used here.
